bridges.name: BluetoothLEBridge
bridges.summary: Bluetooth LE central: scan, connect, discover services and characteristics, read, write and subscribe to notifications. Peripheral ids are GUIDs on Apple platforms and MAC addresses on Android. On Linux every call fails with 501. A peripheral must have been seen in a scan first; otherwise calls on it fail with 404.

bridges.name: CalendarBridge
bridges.summary: The device's calendars, from the page. Android, iOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS and Windows; Linux answers `isNotSupported`. Every call but `getAccess` and `requestAccess` fails with `access_denied` until access has been granted.

requests.summary: Where calendar access stands, without asking.
Asks for access, prompting if the OS has not asked before.
Events overlapping a range of at most 366 days, a page at a time, in start order.
Creates an event. A read-only calendar fails with `read_only`.
Changes only what `changes` sets. An event cannot move between calendars.
Deletes an event — or, with `series`, the rest of the recurring series it belongs to.

bridges.name: CameraBridge
bridges.summary: The device's own camera, driven from wherever the page is — a laptop across the room from a phone on a mount. Not the camera of the machine showing the page: that is `getUserMedia`. The camera runs on a camera screen on the device, and only while one is open: iOS will not run a camera in the background at all. `open` asks the device to show one; until it does, `live` is false and commands fail with 409 (`camera_not_open`), which a page should show as an instruction rather than an error. A command the camera cannot take in its current state — stop a recording that is not running, change lens while recording — fails with 422 (`camera_state`). Linux has no camera: 501. The viewfinder is `GET {bridge}/camera/preview` — a `multipart/x-mixed-replace` MJPEG stream an `` plays directly. The device only encodes frames while someone is watching. Add a changing query parameter each time it is shown, or a browser may reuse the previous, never-ending response.

requests.summary: The camera's state, and whether this platform has one and the app may use it — without prompting.
Prompts for camera access where the platform still will, and says where it stands.
Asks the device to show its camera screen. Answers straight away; the camera arrives on `onStatus` when it is up. Does nothing when one is already open.
Closes the camera screen the bridge opened. A camera screen the app opened itself is the app's to close.
Takes a photo at full resolution and files it.
Starts recording video. The camera has to be in video mode.
Stops recording and files the video.
Changes the live camera, and answers with the state it is in afterwards.

events.summary: The camera changed — opened, closed, switched mode, filed a capture. Raised with the whole state.

bridges.name: ContactsBridge
bridges.summary: The device's address book: search and page through contacts, read one, create, update and delete, and fetch photos. Android and iOS; elsewhere every call fails with 501. Without access, calls fail with 403.

requests.summary: Whether the app has contacts access, without prompting.
Prompts for contacts access if it has not been decided.
A page of contacts ordered by family then given name, optionally matching a name, phone or email.
Creates a contact. It needs a given name, family name or company.
One contact. Fails with 404 when there is no such contact.
Changes the properties set in `changes` and leaves the rest as they are.
Deletes a contact.
The contact's photo as encoded image bytes. Fails with 404 when it has none.

bridges.name: QuickEntryBridge
bridges.summary: Quick entry: a prompt window that opens over other applications — from a global hotkey, a tray click or the page — in the style of Spotlight or a desktop assistant. The page configures the prompt, hears what is submitted, and writes the response back, and it keeps working with the app's own window closed: submissions also go to background.js. Windows, macOS and Linux; Android and iOS fail with 501.

requests.summary: Whether quick entry works here, and what it is doing.
Changes how the window opens. A hotkey another application owns is reported, not an error.
Opens the window.
Closes the window.
Opens the window if it is closed, and closes it if it is open.
The prompt. Fails with 409 when the app replaced the prompt with content of its own.
Changes the prompt: its placeholder, suggestions, busy state and response.
Clears the entry, the response and the busy state.
Lights the glow around the screen's edge until `hideGlow`.
Lights the glow for a while, answering once it has gone out.

The user chose a suggestion, just before it is submitted.
The user pressed Escape in the prompt.
The user pressed the microphone button.
The window opened, however it was opened.
The window closed, however it was dismissed.

bridges.name: TrayBridge
bridges.summary: System tray and menu bar icons on Windows, macOS and Linux: create and update them, give them menus, show notifications, animate them, and hear clicks and menu choices. Android and iOS fail with 501. Ids are 1–64 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`.

Creates an icon, assigning an id when `id` is null. Fails with 429 past the limit.
Removes every icon.
One icon. Fails with 404 when there is no such icon.

Stops animating and restores the icon.

A menu item was chosen. Also delivered to background.js when no page is listening.

bridges.name: DiscoveryBridge
bridges.summary: Local network discovery over mDNS/Bonjour, SSDP/UPnP and WS-Discovery: search for a window, browse with results as events, resolve one, and advertise this app. A protocol the app did not register fails with 501. A browse needs a listener for its protocol's results first — it fails with 409 without one — and stops once that has none left; publications keep advertising until removed or the app exits.

Browses for mDNS services; results arrive through `onMdns`.
Resolves one mDNS service. Fails with 404 when it does not answer.
Advertises a service over mDNS. On iOS the type must be listed in `NSBonjourServices`.
The UPnP devices seen during the scan window, less any that went away.
Browses for UPnP devices; results arrive through `onSsdp`.
A device's UPnP description. The device must have been seen by a search or browse first; otherwise 404.
Advertises a device over SSDP.
The WS-Discovery targets seen during the scan window, less any that went away.
Browses for WS-Discovery targets; results arrive through `onWsd`.
Resolves one WS-Discovery target. Fails with 404 when it does not answer.
Advertises a target over WS-Discovery.
The running browses.

The active publications.
Stops advertising, sending a goodbye so it vanishes from other devices straight away.

A UPnP device was found or lost by a browse.

A browse ended.

bridges.name: DocumentGeofencesBridge
bridges.summary: Document geofencing: GPS-driven monitoring of polygon and proximity regions stored in Shiny.DocumentDb, with no platform limit on how many. The app registers the region sets in C#; the page starts and stops monitoring, reads where the device is, and hears changes. Android, iOS and Mac Catalyst; elsewhere every call fails with 501.

requests.summary: Whether monitoring is running, and the region sets the app registered.
Requests the background location permission monitoring needs.
Starts monitoring; a no-op while it runs. Fails with 409 without permission and with 501 when the store's provider cannot run spatial queries.
Stops monitoring and forgets which regions the device was in.
The region the device is in for each set, from the last GPS reading, without raising changes. Empty when there is no reading.

events.summary: The device entered or left a region, while the page is open.

bridges.name: FoldersBridge
bridges.summary: Folders the user picks with the platform's own picker. A picked folder becomes a file root: the page reads and writes it through `IFilesBridge` under the root name it chose, and it is still there the next time the app runs, until the page forgets it. Where the platform has no folder picker, calls fail with 501.

requests.summary: Whether folders can be picked here, and the folders picked so far.
Shows the folder picker. Null when the user cancels. Picking again under a root name already in use replaces that folder; the app's own roots (`data`, `cache`) cannot be replaced.
Forgets a picked folder: its root goes away and the app gives up its access to it.

bridges.name: GeofencesBridge
bridges.summary: Geofences: monitor circular regions and hear when the device enters or leaves one. Android, iOS, Mac Catalyst and Windows; elsewhere every call fails with 501.

requests.summary: The permission state, without prompting.
Requests the background location permission geofencing needs.
The regions being monitored.
Starts monitoring a region. Fails with 409 without permission.
Stops monitoring every region.
Stops monitoring one region.
Whether the device is inside a monitored region now. Fails with 404 for a region not monitored.

events.summary: The device entered or left a region, while the page is open.

bridges.name: GeocodingBridge
bridges.summary: Reverse geocoding: the addresses at a position, from the platform geocoder (MapKit / CoreLocation on iOS and Mac Catalyst, `android.location.Geocoder` on Android) or, on Windows, Linux, macOS and Android devices without a geocoding backend, OpenStreetMap's Nominatim. It needs network access but no location permission.

requests.summary: The placemarks at a position, most relevant first — empty when the geocoder found nothing. Fails with 400 for a position off the map and 503 when the platform geocoder could not answer (typically no network).

bridges.name: GpsBridge
bridges.summary: GPS: permission, the last and current position, and a listener whose readings arrive as events. Android, iOS, Mac Catalyst and Windows; elsewhere every call fails with 501.

requests.summary: The permission state for a kind of GPS use, without prompting.
Requests the permission the listener settings need — background access for a background mode.
The last known position, or null when there is none.
A fresh position, or null when none could be had.

bridges.name: MotionBridge
bridges.summary: Motion activity: walking, running, cycling, driving or stationary, as the OS's activity recognition reports it. Android, iOS and Mac Catalyst; elsewhere every call fails with 501. There is no history, only the latest reading and live ones.

requests.summary: The permission state, without prompting.
Requests motion activity permission.
The latest reading, or null when there is none.
Whether the listener is running.
Starts listening; readings arrive through `onActivity`, and in the background to the web app's `motion` handler. Fails with 409 without permission.
Stops listening.

events.summary: A reading from the listener, while the page is open.

bridges.name: HealthBridge
bridges.summary: HealthKit on iOS and Health Connect on Android: request access per type, read samples, write them, and watch a type for new readings. Elsewhere every call fails with 501; where the store is missing (Health Connect not installed), with 503; without access to a type, with 403.

requests.summary: Whether the store is available, every type with its unit, and the types being watched.
Requests access to up to 64 types. The platform decides which prompts to show.

Samples in a range of at most 366 days. Numeric types and blood pressure are bucketed by `interval`, at most 2,000 buckets; record types — cycle tracking, workouts, nutrition — are individual records and ignore it.
Writes one sample. Which fields it needs depends on the type; a missing one fails with 400.
Watches a type; readings arrive through `onReading`, so listen first: without a listener it fails with 409. At most 8 types at once. Every watch stops once `onReading` has no listener left.
Stops watching a type. Fails with 404 when it is not being watched.

events.summary: A new reading for a watched type.
Watching a type ended, because it was stopped or it failed.

bridges.name: TransfersBridge
bridges.summary: Background HTTP transfers that keep going while the app is suspended: downloads into a file root and uploads from one. Only the web app's own transfers are listed or cancelled. A download lands at its path only once it completes.

requests.summary: The web app's transfers.

Queues a transfer. Fails with 403 for a URL the app does not allow, 404 for an unknown root or a missing upload file, 409 when a download's destination exists and overwrite is off, 429 when too many are queued.
Cancels every web app transfer, and none of the native app's.
One transfer. Fails with 404 when there is no such transfer.
Cancels a transfer.
Pauses a transfer.
Resumes a paused transfer.

events.summary: A transfer moved on or changed state. Throttled per transfer; a state change always comes through.
A transfer completed; a download is in place at its path.
A transfer failed.
A transfer was cancelled.

bridges.name: InAppPurchasesBridge
bridges.summary:
In-app purchases — consumables, non-consumables and auto-renewable subscriptions — through the App Store (StoreKit 2) on iOS and Google Play Billing on Android. The store's own sheet takes the payment; the page never sees card details.

Verify, grant, then finish: send `verificationData` to your server, store the entitlement, and only then call `finish`. Never grant a `Pending` purchase. Google Play refunds a purchase that is not finished within three days.

Store failures answer with the error code the page switches on: 503 `store_unavailable` or `network`, 403 `not_allowed`, 404 `product_not_found`, 409 `product_unavailable`, `no_user_interface` or `invalid_state`, 400 `developer_error`, and 502 `verification_failed` or `purchase_failed`.

requests.summary: Which store this device buys through, and whether this user may make payments right now.
Localized products and prices. Ids the store does not know are left out rather than failing.

Opens the store's purchase sheet. A cancelled sheet, a pending payment (Ask to Buy, a slow payment method) and a product already owned are results, not errors. A `Success` is not finished: verify and grant it, then call `finish`.
What the user owns now: non-consumables, active subscriptions, and consumables not yet finished.
Purchases that were paid for but never finished — check at startup, and run each through the same verify, grant, finish path, so a crash between payment and finishing never loses a purchase.

Finishes a purchase once its entitlement is stored. `consume` makes a consumable buyable again. The bridge finds the purchase in the store by its transaction id, and fails with 404 (`purchase_not_found`) when the store has no unfinished purchase or entitlement by it — typically because it was finished already.
Restores purchases and returns the entitlements. On iOS this syncs with the App Store and may ask the user to sign in, so call it only from a "Restore Purchases" button.
Opens the store's subscription management screen — on Android, focused on one product when it is named.

events.summary: A purchase changed outside a `purchase` call: an Ask to Buy approval, a pending payment that completed, a renewal, a refund, a purchase on another device, an offer code. The same purchase can arrive more than once, so handle it idempotently by `transactionId`. Also handed to a `purchases.updated` handler, so background.js can verify, grant and finish it when no page is open.

bridges.name: LiveActivitiesBridge
bridges.summary: Live activities: iOS/iPadOS Live Activities on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, and Android 16 Live Updates (an ordinary ongoing notification on older Android). The page decides what an activity says; the app's widget decides how it looks.

requests.summary: Whether the user allows live activities, and the device's push-to-start token when it has one.
Asks for the permission live activities need — notification permission on Android. iOS has no prompt, so it reports the Live Activities switch in Settings.
The activities this app has running, newest first.
Starts an activity. Fails with 502 (`live_activity_failed`) when the system refuses it — the user switched live activities off, or the app has too many running.
Replaces a running activity's content. Fails with 404 when no running activity has the id.
Ends an activity, optionally showing final content until it is dismissed. Fails with 404 when no running activity has the id.
Ends every activity this app has running.

events.summary: An activity started — from this app, or from a push-to-start notification. Also handed to a `liveactivities.started` handler.
An activity became stale, ended or was dismissed. Also handed to a `liveactivities.state` handler.

The system issued or rotated the push token for one activity (iOS). Send it to your server: it is the only way to update that activity remotely. Also handed to a `liveactivities.token` handler, so background.js can send it when no page is open.
The device's push-to-start token appeared or rotated (iOS 17.2+). A server uses it to start an activity while the app is not running. Also handed to a `liveactivities.starttoken` handler.

bridges.name: DirectionsBridge
bridges.summary: Turn-by-turn directions. A route is computed on the device when the user downloaded the road network of a region covering every stop and the platform can run the router, and by the app's online router otherwise. Addresses become stops through the app's geocoder. The router's and the geocoder's addresses and keys stay in the native app; the page never sees them.

requests.summary: Which sources can answer.

Computes a route through the stops. Fails with 400 for fewer than two stops or a stop off the map, 404 when no route connects them, 503 (`offline_unavailable`) when the device cannot compute it and the online router cannot be reached, 501 when neither is available on this platform and app.

Finds places matching an address or a name — "1701 Wynkoop St, Denver", "Red Rocks Amphitheatre" — best first, for turning what the user typed into a `RouteStop`. Always online. Fails with 400 for an empty query or one over 200 characters, 503 (`geocoder_unavailable`) when the geocoder cannot be reached, 501 when the app configured no geocoder.

bridges.name: MapsBridge
bridges.summary: Vector maps the page draws with MapLibre or any other vector-tile renderer. Tiles come from a region the user downloaded when one covers them, and from the app's online source otherwise, so the page asks for one set of URLs and never has to know which. Regions are listed from the app's signed catalog and downloaded on request.

requests.summary: The URLs to hand the renderer, and what the app configured.
The downloadable regions and what is installed. The catalog is fetched again when `refresh` is true or the last copy is old; offline, the last copy is used.

Starts downloading a region — its map, and its road network when asked — or updates an installed one to the catalog's build. Returns at once: `Installed` when the device already has the catalog's build, `Queued` otherwise, with progress arriving as `maps.download` — possibly before this reply does, so a page that tracks progress keeps the newest event rather than this reply. Fails with 404 for a region the catalog does not list, 409 when one is already downloading, 501 when the app configured no catalog.
Removes a region — map and road network — from the device, cancelling its download if one is running.
Removes only a region's road network: the map still draws offline, directions go online.
Cancels a region's download. What was already installed stays.
One vector tile, as MapLibre asks for it through `tilesUrl`. 204 when no source has it — outside every downloaded region while offline.

One live traffic tile, as the renderer asks for it through `tilesUrl`: a vector tile or an image, as `format` says. 204 when the provider has nothing there or cannot be reached; 501 when the app configured no traffic provider.
One live traffic incident tile, as the renderer asks for it through `tilesUrl`. 204 when the provider has nothing there or cannot be reached; 501 when the app configured no incident provider.
A range of label glyphs, as MapLibre asks for it through `glyphsUrl`: `0-255.pbf`.
A sprite sheet or its index, as MapLibre asks for it: `light.json`, `light@2x.png`.

events.summary: A region's download moved on, finished, failed or was cancelled.

bridges.name: NotificationsBridge
bridges.summary: Local notifications: permission, sending now or on a schedule, repeating or on entering an area, the pending list, cancelling, the app badge and Android channels. What a platform can do is in `NotificationStatus`; a feature it lacks fails with 501.

requests.summary: Permission and what this platform supports.
Requests permission, optionally for time-sensitive and location-aware notifications too.
Sends or schedules a notification. Fails with 400 for an invalid one, such as a date already past.
Scheduled notifications that have not been shown yet.
Cancels pending notifications, clears displayed ones, or both.
Cancels one notification.
The app icon's badge number.
Sets the app icon's badge number, 0–99,999.
The notification channels.
Adds or replaces a channel.
Removes a channel.

events.summary: The user tapped a notification, or one of its actions.
A notification arrived while the app was open. Apple platforms only.

bridges.name: ObdBridge
bridges.summary: OBD-II through one ELM327 or OBDLink adapter at a time, over Bluetooth LE or Wi-Fi: find and connect to an adapter, read values, the VIN and trouble codes, and monitor readings live. Calls that need an adapter fail with 409 when none is connected.

requests.summary: The connection, the adapter, Bluetooth availability, and the running monitor.
The named commands `read` and `startMonitor` accept.
The adapters seen during the scan window.
The last scan's adapters.
Connects to an adapter — a Bluetooth peripheral, or a Wi-Fi host, probed when none is given.
Disconnects, stopping the monitor.
Reads one named value. Fails with 404 for a command not in `getCommands`.
Sends a raw request and returns the adapter's reply. Only read-only requests are accepted: OBD modes 01, 02, 03, 05, 06, 07, 09, 0A or 22 in hex, or a harmless AT command.
The vehicle identification number.
Stored, pending and permanent trouble codes.
Clears trouble codes. This also resets the emissions readiness monitors, which take several drive cycles to complete again, so `confirm` must be true.

Reads up to 10 named values on an interval; readings arrive through `onReading`, so listen first: without a listener it fails with 409. The monitor stops once that has no listener left; the adapter stays connected.
Stops the monitor.

events.summary: A monitored reading, or the error reading it.
The adapter went away or stopped answering.

bridges.name: PhotosBridge
bridges.summary: Photos, two ways. The system picker needs no permission — the user chooses — and works on every head. The library is browsing every photo on the device, newest first, with thumbnails; it needs library access and is not available on Linux. Either way a photo reaches the page as a file in a file root, read through `IFilesBridge`.

requests.summary: What works here, and whether the app has library access — without prompting.
Requests photo library access.
Shows the system photo picker and copies what the user chose into a file root. Empty when the user cancels. Not every platform enforces `limit`.
A page of the photo library, newest first. Fails with 403 without library access.
A JPEG thumbnail that fits a square of `size` pixels, 32–1024.
Copies a library photo at full size into a file root.

bridges.name: PrintersBridge
bridges.summary: Receipt and label printers — ESC/POS or TSPL over Bluetooth LE or the network (raw TCP, port 9100), one at a time: find and connect to a printer, then print receipts built in the page. Printing fails with 409 when none is connected. For an office printer, render the same receipt to a PDF and print that through the printing bridge.

requests.summary: The connected printer, and what can be used here.
The printers seen during the scan window: Bluetooth printers matching a known model, or network printers advertising over mDNS (`_pdl-datastream._tcp`, `_printer._tcp`).
Connects to a printer. Fails with 409 while another is connected.
Disconnects the printer.
Prints a receipt on the connected printer.
Renders a receipt as a PDF. Needs no printer.

events.summary: The printer went away.

bridges.name: PrintingBridge
bridges.summary: The operating system's own printing — AirPrint on iOS and Mac Catalyst, the print dialog on Android, the spooler on Windows, CUPS on Linux and macOS — for any printer it knows. A receipt printer needs the printers bridge instead.

requests.summary: What printing can do here.
The installed printers; empty where they cannot be listed.

What ends up in the file differs by platform. Android, macOS, Windows and Linux record the whole screen, other apps included; iOS and Mac Catalyst record only this app. Every platform but Windows asks the user first — a consent dialog, a system permission or the compositor's picker — so `start` can take as long as the user takes to answer.

fields.name: latitude
fields.doc: The GPS position that produced the change.

fields.name: longitude
fields.doc: The GPS position that produced the change.

fields.name: region
fields.doc: The region document as the store serializes it. Null when its type has no JSON metadata in the store's serializer options, or for an exit from a region since deleted.

DocumentRegionSetInfo.summary: A layer of regions the app registered in C# — states, cities, delivery zones.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The name every change in the set carries.

fields.name: withinMeters
fields.doc: Set for a proximity set — inside means within this distance; null for containment.

fields.name: supported
fields.doc: Whether this platform has a folder picker.

fields.name: root
fields.doc: The file root name to give the folder: 1–64 letters, digits, `-` or `_`. One is chosen when null.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: The picker's title, where the platform shows one.

fields.name: root
fields.doc: The file root name the files bridge knows the folder by.

fields.name: displayName
fields.doc: The folder's name as the user saw it in the picker.

fields.name: available
fields.doc: False when the folder was moved, deleted or its access revoked since it was picked.

fields.name: identifier
fields.doc: Names the region; monitoring one with an identifier already in use replaces it.

fields.name: radiusMeters
fields.doc: Must be positive.

fields.name: singleUse
fields.doc: Stop monitoring after the first transition.

GpsAccessMode.summary: Which kind of GPS use a permission check is for.

GpsBackgroundMode.summary: How a listener keeps running with the app in the background.

fields.name: requestPreciseAccuracy
fields.doc: Ask for precise rather than approximate location where the platform distinguishes.

fields.name: autoRestart
fields.doc: Restart the listener after the app is relaunched.

fields.name: positionAccuracy
fields.doc: Meters.

fields.name: heading
fields.doc: Degrees from north.

fields.name: altitude
fields.doc: Meters.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: Meters per second.

Placemark.summary: A human-readable description of a position from the platform geocoder. Any part it could not resolve is null.

fields.name: latitude
fields.doc: The latitude of the position the placemark describes.

fields.name: longitude
fields.doc: The longitude of the position the placemark describes.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The name of the place: a landmark or business, or the street address.

fields.name: subThoroughfare
fields.doc: The street number.

fields.name: thoroughfare
fields.doc: The street name.

fields.name: subLocality
fields.doc: The neighbourhood or district.

fields.name: locality
fields.doc: The city or town.

fields.name: subAdministrativeArea
fields.doc: The county or equivalent.

fields.name: administrativeArea
fields.doc: The state, province or equivalent.

fields.name: postalCode
fields.doc: The postal or zip code.

fields.name: countryCode
fields.doc: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

fields.name: countryName
fields.doc: The localized country name.

fields.name: formattedAddress
fields.doc: The full address on one line, formatted by the platform.

fields.name: granted
fields.doc: Whether the platform reported success. iOS never says whether read access was granted.

HealthDataKind.summary: How a type is read: bucketed numbers, bucketed blood pressure pairs, or individual records.

HealthInterval.summary: The bucket size for numeric and blood pressure reads.

fields.name: pollingIntervalSeconds
fields.doc: How often Android polls, 5–300 seconds. iOS is pushed and ignores it.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Why it ended, when it failed rather than being stopped.

HealthSample.summary: One sample. Which fields are set depends on the type: `value` for numeric types, `systolic` and `diastolic` for blood pressure, and the fields named after each record type for the rest.

HealthSampleInput.summary: A sample to write. `end` defaults to `start`. Set the fields the type needs: `value` for numeric types, `systolic` and `diastolic` for blood pressure, `flow` for menstruation flow, `outcome` for an ovulation test, `workout` for a workout. Numbers must be finite and not negative; title and name at most 256 characters.

fields.name: unit
fields.doc: What values are measured in; null for record types.

fields.name: available
fields.doc: False where the store is missing — Health Connect not installed.

fields.name: listeners
fields.doc: The types being watched.

fields.name: unit
fields.doc: What values are measured in — `count`, `bpm`, `kg`; null for record types.

fields.name: bucketed
fields.doc: Whether reads are bucketed by interval.

TransferBody.summary: An extra form part sent with a multipart upload.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: At most 1 MB.

fields.name: contentType
fields.doc: `text/plain` when null.

fields.name: root
fields.doc: The file root, while the file is inside one.

fields.name: percentComplete
fields.doc: 0–1, when the size is known.

fields.name: statusCode
fields.doc: The server's status, for a failure that had one.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Why it failed.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: An absolute http or https URL. Loopback is refused unless the app allows it.

fields.name: root
fields.doc: The file root a download goes into or an upload comes from.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: The file inside the root.

fields.name: method
fields.doc: GET, POST, PUT or PATCH; the transfer type's default when null.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: At most 32. Hop-by-hop, content and proxy headers are refused.

fields.name: useMeteredConnection
fields.doc: Whether the transfer may run on a metered network.

fields.name: formDataName
fields.doc: The file's form field name for a multipart upload; `file` when null.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: An extra form part, for a multipart upload only.

fields.name: overwrite
fields.doc: Whether a download may replace an existing file.

fields.name: consume
fields.doc: True for a consumable, so it can be bought again; false acknowledges a non-consumable or subscription. Apple has no separate consume step, so this only matters on Google Play — but always say what the product is.

ManageSubscriptionsRequest.summary: Which subscription management screen to open.

fields.name: productId
fields.doc: Android: focus on this subscription. Apple always opens the full list.

PricingPhase.summary: One phase of a subscription's price schedule.

fields.name: displayPrice
fields.doc: The localized, formatted price of one billing period.

fields.name: price
fields.doc: The price of one billing period, as a number.

fields.name: currencyCode
fields.doc: ISO 4217 currency code.

fields.name: billingPeriod
fields.doc: An ISO 8601 duration: `P1W`, `P1M`, `P1Y`.

fields.name: billingCycleCount
fields.doc: How many periods the phase lasts; 0 recurs until cancelled.

fields.name: paymentMode
fields.doc: How the phase is charged.

ProductType.summary: What kind of product it is.

fields.name: productIds
fields.doc: Store product ids, as configured in App Store Connect or the Play Console.

Purchase.summary: A purchase as the device's store reports it.

fields.name: platform
fields.doc: The store it was made through.

fields.name: productId
fields.doc: The store product id.

fields.name: transactionId
fields.doc: Unique per charge — finish it by this. Apple: the transaction id, new on each renewal. Google: the order id, or the purchase token while the purchase is pending.

fields.name: originalTransactionId
fields.doc: Stable across renewals. Apple: the original transaction id. Google: the purchase token.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: Purchased, pending or revoked.

fields.name: purchaseDate
fields.doc: When it — or this renewal — was bought.

fields.name: expirationDate
fields.doc: Apple subscriptions only; Google does not report expiry on the device, so ask your server.

fields.name: isFinished
fields.doc: Apple: finished. Google: acknowledged or consumed.

fields.name: isAutoRenewing
fields.doc: A subscription set to renew.

fields.name: quantity
fields.doc: Units bought.

fields.name: accountToken
fields.doc: The `accountToken` it was bought with.

fields.name: verificationData
fields.doc: Send this to your server to verify the purchase. Apple: the signed JWS transaction. Google: the purchase token. Shiny.Mobile.InAppPurchases.Server's `IPurchaseVerifier` takes it as it is.

fields.name: appId
fields.doc: The bundle id (Apple) or package name (Google).

fields.name: environment
fields.doc: The store environment; always Unknown on Google Play.

fields.name: originalJson
fields.doc: The store's raw JSON for the transaction.

fields.name: signature
fields.doc: Google Play: the RSA signature of `originalJson`. Null on Apple.

fields.name: revocationDate
fields.doc: Apple: when it was refunded or revoked.

fields.name: productId
fields.doc: The store product id.

fields.name: accountToken
fields.doc: Your user's id. It comes back on every transaction and in the stores' server notifications (Apple `appAccountToken`, Google `obfuscatedAccountId`), so your server can tell whose purchase it is. Always set it.

fields.name: offerToken
fields.doc: Google Play: the `offerToken` to buy; the first base plan when omitted. Ignored on Apple.

fields.name: quantity
fields.doc: Apple: how many units of a consumable, 1 to 10. Google lets the user choose in the sheet when the product allows it.

fields.name: replacement
fields.doc: Google Play: the subscription this one replaces. Ignored on Apple.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: What happened.

fields.name: purchase
fields.doc: Set on `Success`, and on `Pending` when the store reports one.

PurchasesStatus.summary: The store this device buys through, and whether it can buy now.

fields.name: platform
fields.doc: App Store or Google Play.

fields.name: canMakePayments
fields.doc: False when the store is unreachable or payments are blocked — parental controls, MDM, an unsupported country, no Play Store.

StoreEnvironment.summary: Which store environment a purchase was made in.

StorePlatform.summary: The store a device buys through.

StoreProduct.summary: A localized product from the store.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The store product id.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: One-time purchase or subscription.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: The localized name.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: The localized description.

fields.name: displayPrice
fields.doc: The localized, formatted price — for a subscription, the recurring price of its default plan.

fields.name: price
fields.doc: The price as a number, in `currencyCode`.

fields.name: currencyCode
fields.doc: ISO 4217 currency code.

fields.name: subscriptionOffers
fields.doc: Google Play: one per base plan and per offer the user is eligible for; buy one with its `offerToken`. Apple: the introductory offer when the user is eligible, then promotional offers.

fields.name: subscriptionGroupId
fields.doc: Apple's subscription group; null on Google Play and for one-time products.

SubscriptionOffer.summary: A subscription base plan or offer.

fields.name: offerId
fields.doc: Apple's offer id or Google's; null for an Apple introductory offer and a Google base plan.

fields.name: basePlanId
fields.doc: Google's base plan id; null on Apple.

fields.name: offerToken
fields.doc: Google Play: pass it as `offerToken` to buy this offer. Null on Apple.

fields.name: isIntroductory
fields.doc: An Apple introductory offer, or a Google free trial or introductory price.

fields.name: pricingPhases
fields.doc: The price schedule in order — a free trial, then the recurring price.

fields.name: tags
fields.doc: Google offer tags; empty on Apple.

SubscriptionPaymentMode.summary: How a subscription pricing phase is charged.

SubscriptionReplacement.summary: Replaces a Google Play subscription with another — an upgrade or downgrade. Apple changes plans within a subscription group itself.

fields.name: oldProductId
fields.doc: The subscription being replaced.

fields.name: oldPurchaseToken
fields.doc: Its purchase token: the old purchase's `originalTransactionId`.

fields.name: mode
fields.doc: How the change is prorated and charged.

SubscriptionReplacementMode.summary: How a Google Play subscription change is prorated and charged.

LiveActivitiesStatus.summary: Whether this app can show live activities.

fields.name: access
fields.doc: The iOS Live Activities switch for this app, or notification permission on Android.

fields.name: pushToStartToken
fields.doc: The device's push-to-start token (iOS 17.2+); null on Android, older iOS, and until the system issues one.

LiveActivity.summary: A running, or recently ended, live activity.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The system's id, which updates and ends it.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: Where it is in its life.

fields.name: pushToken
fields.doc: The token that addresses it from a server, once the system issued one (iOS).

LiveActivityAlert.summary: Turns an update into a banner, and a tap on a paired watch, instead of a silent refresh.

LiveActivityContent.summary: What an activity says — everything that can change while it runs.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: The headline: "Arriving in 5 min", the team names.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: Detail under the title.

fields.name: shortStatus
fields.doc: A few characters for the tightest places — the compact Dynamic Island and the Android 16 status bar chip: "5 min", "2-1".

fields.name: progress
fields.doc: An optional progress bar.

fields.name: staleDate
fields.doc: When this content goes out of date; the activity turns `Stale` then.

fields.name: relevanceScore
fields.doc: Ranks this activity against the app's others when several run (iOS).

fields.name: data
fields.doc: Strings for the app's own widget to read.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: Final content to show until it is dismissed; the last content when omitted.

fields.name: dismissAt
fields.doc: When to take it off screen; the system decides when omitted, and a past time removes it now.

LiveActivityProgress.summary: A progress bar. Set `value`, or `start` and `end` for a timer the system advances itself, or `indeterminate`.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The completed fraction, 0 to 1.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: The start of a time range the system animates between.

fields.name: end
fields.doc: The end of that range.

fields.name: indeterminate
fields.doc: Progress of unknown length.

fields.name: activityId
fields.doc: The activity it addresses.

fields.name: token
fields.doc: The APNs token, hex.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: What it says first.

fields.name: attributes
fields.doc: What never changes for its lifetime — an order number, the teams. A push-to-start payload names the same attributes.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Which layout renders it, for an app whose widget has more than one.

fields.name: requestPushToken
fields.doc: Ask for a push token so a server can update it; it arrives as `liveactivities.token`. On iOS the app needs the `aps-environment` entitlement for this, or the start fails.

LiveActivityState.summary: Where a live activity is in its life.

LiveActivityUpdateRequest.summary: New content for a running activity.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: Replaces what it says.

fields.name: alert
fields.doc: Alert the user about the change; silent when omitted.

fields.name: online
fields.doc: Whether the app configured an online router.

fields.name: onDevice
fields.doc: Whether this platform can compute routes on the device. It still needs a downloaded road network to do so.

fields.name: offlineRegions
fields.doc: The regions whose road network is on the device.

fields.name: geocoding
fields.doc: Whether the app configured a geocoder, so `geocode` can turn an address into a stop.

fields.name: stops
fields.doc: Two or more, in order: where the route starts, any stops along the way, where it ends.

fields.name: language
fields.doc: An IETF language tag for the instructions, such as `en-US` or `fr`. English when null or unsupported.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: Where the route was computed: `Device` or `Online`.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: Metres.

fields.name: duration
fields.doc: Seconds.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The line to draw, as `[longitude, latitude]` pairs — GeoJSON's order, so it drops into a LineString as it is.

fields.name: bounds
fields.doc: `[west, south, east, north]` around `shape`, for fitting the map to the route.

DistanceUnits.summary: The units spoken and written instructions use. Distances in the response are always metres.

fields.name: places
fields.doc: Best match first. Empty when nothing matched.

fields.name: attribution
fields.doc: The credit the geocoder's terms require, as HTML.

GeocodedPlace.summary: A place a geocoder found for an address or a name.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: What the place is called: "Union Station", "1701 Wynkoop Street".

fields.name: address
fields.doc: The full address or description, which tells apart places with the same name.

fields.name: bounds
fields.doc: `[west, south, east, north]` around a place with an extent — a city, a park — for fitting the map to it. Null for a point.

ManeuverKind.summary: What a maneuver asks the traveller to do. Enough to pick an arrow icon.

fields.name: regions
fields.doc: The catalog's regions, and any installed region the catalog no longer lists.

fields.name: catalogReachable
fields.doc: False when the catalog could not be fetched — offline, say. The regions are then the ones last seen and the ones installed.

fields.name: installedBytes
fields.doc: Disk space the installed regions take.

MapPackDownload.summary: A region's download. Raised as `maps.download` while it runs and once more when it ends.

fields.name: directions
fields.doc: Whether the download includes the road network.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Why it failed.

fields.name: directions
fields.doc: Also download the road network, so directions inside the region work offline. Ignored when the region does not offer it.

MapRegion.summary: A region the page can download, merged with what is on the device.

fields.name: bounds
fields.doc: `[west, south, east, north]` in degrees.

fields.name: mapSize
fields.doc: Bytes to download for the map tiles.

fields.name: directionsSize
fields.doc: Bytes to download for on-device directions, when the region offers them.

fields.name: mapInstalled
fields.doc: Whether the region's map is on the device, so it draws offline.

fields.name: directionsInstalled
fields.doc: Whether the region's road network is on the device, so directions inside it work offline.

fields.name: updateAvailable
fields.doc: Whether the catalog has a newer build of an installed part.

fields.name: download
fields.doc: The download in progress for this region, if any.

MapsInfo.summary: Everything a map renderer needs to draw from the bridge. The URLs are templates MapLibre (or any vector-tile renderer) fills in itself, relative to the page's origin and already under the bridge's prefix.

fields.name: tilesUrl
fields.doc: The vector tiles: `…/maps/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}`. Served from a downloaded region when one covers the tile, from the online source otherwise.

fields.name: glyphsUrl
fields.doc: The label fonts: `…/maps/glyphs/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf`.

fields.name: spritesUrl
fields.doc: The icon sheets. Append a flavor — `light`, `dark`, `white`, `grayscale`, `black` — for MapLibre's `sprite`.

fields.name: maxZoom
fields.doc: The highest zoom the tiles carry. The renderer draws closer zooms by scaling these, which vector tiles do cleanly.

fields.name: online
fields.doc: Whether the app configured an online tile source. Without one, only downloaded regions draw.

fields.name: catalog
fields.doc: Whether the app configured a region catalog to download from.

fields.name: attribution
fields.doc: The credit the map data's licence requires, as HTML.

fields.name: traffic
fields.doc: The live traffic layer, when the app configured a traffic provider. Null otherwise.

fields.name: incidents
fields.doc: Live traffic incidents — accidents, roadworks, closures — when the app configured an incident provider. Null otherwise.

RouteLeg.summary: The part of a route between two consecutive stops.

fields.name: instruction
fields.doc: Written for reading: "Turn right onto North Broadway."

fields.name: verbalInstruction
fields.doc: Written for speaking before the maneuver, when the router provides it.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: Metres from this maneuver to the next.

fields.name: duration
fields.doc: Seconds from this maneuver to the next.

fields.name: shapeIndex
fields.doc: Where the maneuver is: an index into `shape`.

fields.name: roundaboutExit
fields.doc: Which exit to take, for `EnterRoundabout`.

TrafficIncidentInfo.summary: A live layer of traffic incidents, whatever provider is behind it: vector tiles holding the stretch of road an incident affects as lines, where it is as points, or both. Tiles come through the bridge, which holds the provider's key, and only while online.

fields.name: tilesUrl
fields.doc: The incident tiles: `…/maps/incidents/{z}/{x}/{y}`.

fields.name: minZoom
fields.doc: Below this the layer draws nothing, and no tiles are asked for.

fields.name: maxZoom
fields.doc: The highest zoom the provider has. The renderer scales past it.

fields.name: refreshSeconds
fields.doc: How often the page should fetch the tiles again.

fields.name: lineSourceLayer
fields.doc: The layer inside each tile holding the affected stretches of road. Null when the provider has none.

fields.name: pointSourceLayer
fields.doc: The layer inside each tile holding incident locations. Null when the provider has none.

fields.name: kindProperty
fields.doc: The property holding the provider's incident type.

fields.name: kinds
fields.doc: The provider's values of `kindProperty`, as text, and what each is. Anything not listed is `Other`.

fields.name: descriptionProperty
fields.doc: The property holding a description to show for an incident. Null when there is none.

fields.name: delayProperty
fields.doc: The property holding the delay the incident causes, in seconds. Null when there is none.

fields.name: clusterSizeProperty
fields.doc: The property holding how many incidents a point stands for, where the provider groups them. Null when it does not.

fields.name: attribution
fields.doc: The credit the provider's terms require, as HTML.

TrafficIncidentKind.summary: What a traffic incident is, whatever each provider calls it. The map colours incidents by it.

TrafficInfo.summary: A live traffic layer, whatever provider is behind it. Tiles come through the bridge, which holds the provider's key, and only while online: offline the layer is simply empty.

fields.name: tilesUrl
fields.doc: The traffic tiles: `…/maps/traffic/{z}/{x}/{y}`.

fields.name: minZoom
fields.doc: Below this the layer draws nothing, and no tiles are asked for.

fields.name: maxZoom
fields.doc: The highest zoom the provider has. The renderer scales past it.

fields.name: refreshSeconds
fields.doc: How often the provider's data changes, so how often the page should fetch the tiles again.

fields.name: sourceLayer
fields.doc: Vector: the layer inside each tile holding the road segments.

fields.name: speedRatioProperty
fields.doc: Vector: the property holding current speed over free-flow speed, from 0 (stopped) to 1 (free flow).

fields.name: closedProperty
fields.doc: Vector: the property that is true on a closed road. Null when the provider does not mark closures.

fields.name: tileSize
fields.doc: Raster: the images' size in pixels.

fields.name: attribution
fields.doc: The credit the provider's terms require, as HTML.

TrafficTileFormat.summary: How a traffic provider's tiles are drawn.

fields.name: identifier
fields.doc: 1–64 letters, digits, `.`, `-` or `_`.

NotificationEvent.summary: A notification the user tapped or that arrived while the app was open.

fields.name: action
fields.doc: The action chosen, when the user picked one rather than the notification itself.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: What the user typed, for a text reply action.

NotificationGeofence.summary: Show the notification when the device enters an area.

NotificationRepeat.summary: A repeating schedule: every `intervalSeconds`, or at `timeOfDay`, optionally on one day.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: At most 4,000 characters.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Replaces a notification with the same id; assigned when null.

fields.name: channel
fields.doc: An Android channel identifier.

fields.name: thread
fields.doc: Groups notifications together.

fields.name: scheduleDate
fields.doc: Show it then rather than now.

fields.name: image
fields.doc: A .png, .jpg, .gif or .heic of at most 10 MB in a file root.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: Comes back on the tap.

fields.name: badge
fields.doc: Whether the app badge can be read and set.

fields.name: entry
fields.doc: Whether taps are reported.

fields.name: received
fields.doc: Whether notifications arriving while the app is open are reported.

fields.name: geofences
fields.doc: Whether a notification can wait for the device to enter an area.

fields.name: images
fields.doc: Whether a notification can carry an image.

fields.name: fromWebApp
fields.doc: Whether the web app sent it, rather than the native app.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: A Bluetooth peripheral id, or a Wi-Fi adapter's host and port.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Such as `engineRpm`.

fields.name: pid
fields.doc: The raw request it sends.

ObdConnectRequest.summary: An adapter to connect to: `peripheralUuid` for Bluetooth, `host` and `port` for Wi-Fi.

fields.name: serviceUuid
fields.doc: For an adapter that does not use the usual GATT service.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Why the reading failed; the value is null then.

fields.name: intervalMs
fields.doc: 250–60,000 ms; one second when null.

fields.name: raw
fields.doc: Such as `010C` or `AT RV`.

fields.name: command
fields.doc: A name from the command list, such as `engineRpm`.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: A numeric reading.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: A text reading.

fields.name: scanMs
fields.doc: Up to 30,000 ms; 5 seconds when null.

fields.name: nameFilter
fields.doc: Only adapters whose name contains this; at most 64 characters.

fields.name: adapterIdentifier
fields.doc: What the adapter reports about itself.

fields.name: protocol
fields.doc: The vehicle protocol the adapter settled on.

fields.name: bluetoothSupported
fields.doc: Whether Bluetooth LE adapters can be used here.

fields.name: monitor
fields.doc: The running monitor.

ObdTroubleCodes.summary: Each list is null where the vehicle did not answer that request.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Pass to `getThumbnail` and `export`.

fields.name: root
fields.doc: The file root the photo is copied into.

PhotoFile.summary: A photo copied into a file root.

fields.name: file
fields.doc: Where it is: read it through the files bridge.

fields.name: fileName
fields.doc: The name it had on the device, where the platform says.

fields.name: hasMore
fields.doc: Whether another page follows.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: How many the user may choose, 1–50.

fields.name: root
fields.doc: The file root the photos are copied into.

fields.name: pickerSupported
fields.doc: Whether the system photo picker is available.

fields.name: librarySupported
fields.doc: Whether the photo library can be browsed here.

fields.name: libraryAccess
fields.doc: Library access. `Restricted` is a limited selection the user chose on iOS or Android.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The Bluetooth peripheral id, or `host:port` on the network.

DiscoveredPrinter.summary: A printer a scan found. Connect with its `id`.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The Bluetooth peripheral id, or `host:port` on the network.

fields.name: profile
fields.doc: The known printer model a Bluetooth printer matched.

fields.name: capabilities
fields.doc: What the printer is assumed to be. A network printer never says how wide its paper is, so it is assumed 80mm: pass `paper` when you know better.

PrintElementType.summary: What a `PrintElement` does. Each reads only the fields its description names.

PrintQrCorrection.summary: How much of a QR code can be damaged and still read: about 7, 15, 25 or 30%.

PrintReceiptRequest.summary: A receipt for the connected printer.

fields.name: bytes
fields.doc: What was sent to the printer.

PrintRenderRequest.summary: A receipt to render as a PDF, for a printer that speaks no ESC/POS — an office printer through the printing bridge, or a download — on pages of `pageWidth` by `pageHeight` points.

fields.name: paper
fields.doc: The receipt width images are fitted to; the connected printer's, or 80mm, when null.

fields.name: pageWidth
fields.doc: Points; A4's 595 when null.

fields.name: pageHeight
fields.doc: Points; A4's 842 when null.

fields.name: margin
fields.doc: Points; 36 when null.

fields.name: fontSize
fields.doc: Points; 12 when null.

PrinterCapabilities.summary: What a printer can do. Lay a receipt out against these, never against a fixed width: `charactersPerLine` columns of text, and images up to `dotsPerLine` wide.

fields.name: charactersPerLineFontB
fields.doc: Columns in the smaller font.

fields.name: paperWidthMm
fields.doc: The printable width.

PrinterConnectRequest.summary: The printer to connect to: the `id` of a printer the last scan found, or one named outright — a Bluetooth `peripheralUuid` with its `serviceUuid` and `writeCharacteristicUuid`, or a network `host` (an IP address on the local network) and `port` (9100).

fields.name: paper
fields.doc: The paper width; the scanned printer's, or 80mm on the network and 58mm over Bluetooth, when null.

fields.name: capabilities
fields.doc: Everything about the printer, for one that neither preset describes. Wins over `paper`.

fields.name: language
fields.doc: The scanned printer's, or ESC/POS, when null.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The label stock, for TSPL.

fields.name: timeoutMs
fields.doc: Up to 60,000 ms; 15 seconds when null.

fields.name: chunkSize
fields.doc: Bytes per Bluetooth write, 20–512; the connection's MTU when null. Lower it when a cheap printer garbles a long receipt.

fields.name: chunkDelayMs
fields.doc: A pause between Bluetooth writes, 0–500 ms, to let a small buffer drain.

fields.name: widthMm
fields.doc: 50 when null.

fields.name: heightMm
fields.doc: 30 when null.

fields.name: gapMm
fields.doc: The gap between labels; 3 when null.

PrinterLanguage.summary: The command language the printer speaks: ESC/POS for receipt printers, TSPL for label printers.

PrinterPaper.summary: The common receipt widths: 58mm is 32 columns and 384 dots, 80mm is 48 columns and 576 dots with a cutter.

fields.name: scanMs
fields.doc: Up to 30,000 ms; 5 seconds when null.

fields.name: printer
fields.doc: The connected printer, if any.

fields.name: bluetoothSupported
fields.doc: Whether Bluetooth LE printers can be used here.

fields.name: networkScanSupported
fields.doc: Whether network printers can be found by scanning; one can always be connected by address.

fields.name: renderSupported
fields.doc: Whether `POST render` can turn a receipt into a PDF here.

HtmlToPdfRequest.summary: An HTML document to lay out on pages with the platform's own engine — the one printing uses — and return as a PDF.

fields.name: html
fields.doc: A complete HTML document.

fields.name: pageWidth
fields.doc: Portrait page width in points; A4's 595 when null. Letter is 612.

fields.name: pageHeight
fields.doc: Portrait page height in points; A4's 842 when null. Letter is 792.

fields.name: orientation
fields.doc: `Landscape` swaps width and height; anything else is portrait.

fields.name: margin
fields.doc: A uniform margin in points; 36 (half an inch) when null. A CSS `@page { margin }` in the document wins on Android.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Pass back as `printerId`.

fields.name: jobName
fields.doc: What the print queue shows.

fields.name: silent
fields.doc: Print without the dialog where `silent`; the dialog shows anyway elsewhere.

fields.name: printerId
fields.doc: The printer for a silent job; the default printer when null.

fields.name: copies
fields.doc: 1–99; one when null.

PrintJobRequest.summary: One document: `data` as base64 for a PDF or a PNG/JPEG image, `html` for markup, or `url` for an http or https page.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Why, when `status` is failed.

PrintJobStatus.summary: `Completed` and `Submitted` both mean it printed, or will: submitted is a job handed to a spooler whose end the platform does not report.

PrintingCapabilities.summary: What printing can do here. Feature-detect with these rather than printing to find out.

fields.name: systemDialog
fields.doc: Printing shows the platform's print dialog, where the person picks the printer.

fields.name: silent
fields.doc: A job with `silent` skips the dialog: Windows and CUPS (Linux, macOS).

fields.name: listPrinters
fields.doc: Installed printers can be listed and named in `printerId`.

fields.name: htmlToPdf
fields.doc: HTML can be laid out on pages and returned as a PDF, with no print UI: iOS, Mac Catalyst and Android.

PushPayload.summary: A push as the web app sees it.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: The push's data fields.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: The visible notification's title, when the push carried one.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: The visible notification's body, when the push carried one.

fields.name: access
fields.doc: Whether the app may receive pushes.

fields.name: token
fields.doc: The provider's token — what a server sends to. Null until registered.

fields.name: nativeToken
fields.doc: The platform's own token (APNs, FCM) where it differs from `token`.

PushTags.summary: The tags a device is registered with.

PushTokenEvent.summary: A token that was issued or unregistered.

RpiCameraCapture.summary: A photograph to take and write into a file root.

fields.name: root
fields.doc: The file root, as the files bridge names it.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: Where in the root. An existing file is replaced.

fields.name: cameraId
fields.doc: Null takes the first camera.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Zero takes the bridge's still size.

fields.name: quality
fields.doc: JPEG quality, 1 to 100; zero takes the bridge's still quality.

RpiCameraControl.summary: A sensor control. Which ones exist depends on the module: a Camera Module 3 has autofocus, a v2 doesn't.

fields.name: supported
fields.doc: False when the attached sensor doesn't have the control.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The value the bridge applies to every session it opens; null when it leaves the sensor's own.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Null goes back to the sensor's own value from the next session.

RpiCameraControlsInput.summary: Control values to apply now, to a running stream, and to every session opened later.

RpiCameraInfo.summary: A camera attached to the device.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Stable across reboots, but not across a move to another CSI port.

fields.name: model
fields.doc: The sensor, such as `imx708`; empty when it doesn't say.

fields.name: maxWidth
fields.doc: The full width of the sensor's pixel array.

fields.name: rotationDegrees
fields.doc: How the sensor is mounted.

RpiCameraStatus.summary: What the camera can do here.

fields.name: supported
fields.doc: False off Linux, without libcamera, or with the native shim missing — `backend` says which.

fields.name: backend
fields.doc: The backend and the libcamera it was built against, or why there is none.

fields.name: cameras
fields.doc: Every camera attached. Empty isn't an error: a badly seated ribbon cable looks like this.

fields.name: streams
fields.doc: Streams running now.

RpiCameraStream.summary: A live stream, shared by everyone watching it.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: What the camera actually delivers, which may differ from what was asked for.

fields.name: pixelFormat
fields.doc: The sensor's format as a FourCC, such as `NV12`; frames are encoded to JPEG from it.

fields.name: viewers
fields.doc: Open `stream` responses.

fields.name: framesDropped
fields.doc: Frames the camera produced faster than they could be sent.

ScreenRecorderAccessRequest.summary: Which audio to ask for along with the screen. Only the microphone has a permission of its own.

fields.name: access
fields.doc: Where recording stands after asking. Android cannot grant the screen ahead of time, so it reports `Unknown` there and asks when a recording starts: anything but `Denied` is worth trying.

ScreenRecorderCapability.summary: What this device's recorder can do. A request that asks for something missing here answers 501 rather than recording without it.

ScreenRecorderStatus.summary: The recorder as it is right now.

fields.name: supported
fields.doc: Whether this device can record its screen at all.

fields.name: capabilities
fields.doc: What it can do.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: Where it is.

fields.name: elapsedSeconds
fields.doc: How much has been recorded, without any paused span. Null when nothing is recording.

fields.name: maxDurationSeconds
fields.doc: The longest a recording may run on this device; a longer request is shortened to it.

fields.name: lastRecording
fields.doc: The most recent recording the bridge filed.

ScreenRecording.summary: A recording, filed into a file root and read through the files bridge.

fields.name: file
fields.doc: Where it was filed.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: Bytes.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Encoded width in pixels.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: Encoded height in pixels.

fields.name: durationSeconds
fields.doc: How long it runs, without any paused span.

fields.name: mimeType
fields.doc: What was written — `video/mp4` on every native platform.

ScreenRecordingEnded.summary: A recording ended — stopped, cancelled, or ended by the device.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why.

fields.name: recording
fields.doc: The recording, when there was one to file.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: What went wrong, when something did.

ScreenRecordingRequest.summary: What to record. Every setting but the audio is optional, and each one needs its `ScreenRecorderCapability`: a request for something this device cannot do answers 501.

fields.name: includeMicrophone
fields.doc: Mix in the microphone. Needs `Microphone`.

fields.name: includeSystemAudio
fields.doc: Capture what the device is playing. Needs `SystemAudio`.

fields.name: showCursor
fields.doc: Draw the pointer. Null or true draws it; false needs `CursorToggle`.

fields.name: frameRate
fields.doc: A ceiling, 1–240. Needs `FrameRateControl`.

fields.name: videoBitrate
fields.doc: Bits a second. Needs `BitrateControl`.

fields.name: maxWidth
fields.doc: Downscale to at most this many pixels wide. Needs `Downscaling`.

fields.name: maxDurationSeconds
fields.doc: Stop and file it after this long. Never longer than `maxDurationSeconds`, which also applies when this is null.

AccessState.summary: Where a permission stands. Reported by every bridge that needs one; the names match Shiny's own.

AppLink.summary: A link the app was opened with.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: The link as the OS delivered it.

fields.name: route
fields.doc: The page route it maps to — always a local path, safe to navigate to as it is.

fields.name: receivedAt
fields.doc: When the app received it.

ApplyUpdateResult.summary: The outcome of applying an update.

fields.name: applied
fields.doc: False when nothing was waiting.

fields.name: version
fields.doc: The version now being served, when one was applied.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Its path under the bridge prefix — `calendar` for `/_bridge/calendar`.

fields.name: isSupported
fields.doc: False where the platform has no implementation; its endpoints then answer 501.

BridgeFile.summary: A file the page can reach through the files bridge: a named root and a path inside it. Bridges that take or return a file use this, so nothing reaches the page that `/_bridge/files` would not also serve.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The entry's name; the root's name for the root itself.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: Relative to the root, with forward slashes. Empty for the root.

fields.name: isDirectory
fields.doc: Whether it is a directory.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: Bytes, for files.

fields.name: modified
fields.doc: When it last changed.

fields.name: root
fields.doc: The root's name.

fields.name: change
fields.doc: What happened to it.

FileTransfer.summary: A move or copy within a root.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: The entry to move or copy.

fields.name: to
fields.doc: Where it goes, including its new name.

fields.name: overwrite
fields.doc: Replace an existing file at `to`. Directories are never merged or replaced.

fields.name: appId
fields.doc: The app's id, as the update server knows it.

fields.name: hostVersion
fields.doc: The native app's version.

fields.name: platform
fields.doc: android, ios, maccatalyst, macos, windows or linux.

fields.name: webAppVersion
fields.doc: The web app build being served; null while pages come from a dev server.

fields.name: webAppOrigin
fields.doc: Whether that build is the baseline or a download.

fields.name: pendingVersion
fields.doc: A downloaded update waiting for `applyUpdate`.

fields.name: bridges
fields.doc: Every registered bridge.

fields.name: devServer
fields.doc: The dev server pages are proxied from, in a debug build that uses one.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: The scope listed.

fields.name: encrypted
fields.doc: Whether values in this scope are encrypted at rest on this device.

fields.name: keys
fields.doc: The keys this web app has set, in ordinal order.

SettingsScope.summary: Which store a setting lives in.

WebAppOrigin.summary: Where the web app being served came from.

fields.name: culture
fields.doc: A culture name such as `en-US`; the device's when null.

fields.name: silenceTimeoutMs
fields.doc: How much quiet ends it, 500–10,000 ms.

fields.name: timeoutMs
fields.doc: The longest it waits in all, 1,000–60,000 ms; 15 seconds when null.

fields.name: preferOnDevice
fields.doc: Keep audio on the device where the platform allows.

fields.name: keywords
fields.doc: At most 32, each at most 64 characters.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: What was heard; null when nothing was.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: At most 4,000 characters.

fields.name: culture
fields.doc: A culture name such as `en-US`.

fields.name: voice
fields.doc: A voice's `id`.

fields.name: wait
fields.doc: Return once speech ends rather than straight away.

fields.name: completed
fields.doc: False when it was interrupted.

fields.name: culture
fields.doc: A culture name such as `en-US`; the device's when null.

fields.name: silenceTimeoutMs
fields.doc: How much quiet ends a phrase, 500–10,000 ms.

fields.name: preferOnDevice
fields.doc: Keep audio on the device where the platform allows.

fields.name: keywords
fields.doc: Words that raise `onKeyword`. At most 32, each at most 64 characters.

fields.name: confidence
fields.doc: 0–1, where the platform reports one.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: The context.

fields.name: binary
fields.doc: It was not JSON: `data` is its bytes as a base64 string.

fields.name: nodeId
fields.doc: The node that shared it; null for this app's own.

fields.name: sent
fields.doc: What this app last shared, or null.

fields.name: received
fields.doc: What the wearable last shared, or null.

WearableFileRequest.summary: A file to queue for the wearable.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: What it is — `maps/offline`.

fields.name: file
fields.doc: The file, in a root on disk.

fields.name: metadata
fields.doc: Strings the companion app receives with it.

WearableMessage.summary: A live message from the wearable.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: What it is about.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: The body.

fields.name: binary
fields.doc: The body was not JSON: `data` is its bytes as a base64 string.

fields.name: nodeId
fields.doc: The node that sent it.

fields.name: expectsReply
fields.doc: The sender waits on a reply — what a `wearables.message` handler returns.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: What it is about — `sync`, `workout/start`.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: The body, any JSON value. Keep it small: about 64 KB on iOS, 100 KB on Wear OS.

fields.name: nodeId
fields.doc: Wear OS only: the node to send to. Omitted, the nearby node that runs the companion app.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The node id — always `watch` on iOS, which has one active watch.

fields.name: displayName
fields.doc: The name the platform gives it.

fields.name: isNearby
fields.doc: Directly connected rather than reached through the cloud.

fields.name: hasApp
fields.doc: Runs the companion app.

WearablePendingTransfer.summary: An outgoing transfer or file the wearable has not received yet.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The id the send returned.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: What it is.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Data or a file.

fields.name: progress
fields.doc: 0–1 where the platform reports it (iOS files); null otherwise.

WearableReceivedFile.summary: A file from the wearable, filed into a file root.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The sender's transfer id.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: What the sender said it is.

fields.name: fileName
fields.doc: The file's name on the sender.

fields.name: file
fields.doc: Where it is now — read, move or delete it through the files bridge.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: Its size in bytes.

fields.name: metadata
fields.doc: The strings sent with it.

fields.name: nodeId
fields.doc: The node that sent it.

WearableReply.summary: The companion app's reply to a message.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: The reply; JSON null when the companion app replied with nothing.

fields.name: binary
fields.doc: The reply was not JSON: `data` is its bytes as a base64 string.

WearableStatus.summary: Whether there is a wearable to talk to.

fields.name: supported
fields.doc: False where the platform has no wearable API — anything but iOS and Android, an iPad, an Android device without the Wear OS app.

fields.name: paired
fields.doc: A wearable is paired (iOS) or connected (Android).

fields.name: appInstalled
fields.doc: The companion app is installed on it.

fields.name: reachable
fields.doc: A live message can be sent now. Context, transfers and files queue and do not need this.

fields.name: nodes
fields.doc: The wearables the platform reports.

WearableTransfer.summary: A queued transfer from the wearable.

WearableTransferCompleted.summary: An outgoing transfer or file finished.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The id the send returned.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: What it was; empty on Wear OS, where the delivery receipt carries only the id.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Data or a file.

fields.name: succeeded
fields.doc: The wearable received it.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Why it failed or was cancelled; null when delivered.

WearableTransferRequest.summary: Data to queue for the wearable.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: What it is.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: Any JSON value.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: What `wearables.completed` and the pending list report it by.

fields.name: current
fields.doc: The hotspot now; null when it stopped.

HotspotClient.summary: A device connected to the hotspot.

HotspotStartRequest.summary: A hotspot to start. Every field is optional.

fields.name: supported
fields.doc: Whether the platform supports a hotspot and the app registered it.

fields.name: running
fields.doc: Whether one this app started is running.

fields.name: current
fields.doc: The hotspot, when one is running.

KnownWifiNetwork.summary: A network saved on the device.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: An int on Android, a UUID on Linux, the SSID itself on Apple platforms.

WifiCapability.summary: Something a platform's Wi-Fi can do.

fields.name: current
fields.doc: The network now; null when the device left Wi-Fi.

WifiConnectRequest.summary: A network to join: by `ssid`, or a saved one by `knownNetworkId`.

fields.name: bssid
fields.doc: Join this access point in particular.

fields.name: remember
fields.doc: Save the network on the device.

fields.name: timeoutMs
fields.doc: How long to wait for the connection, in milliseconds; the platform's default when null.

fields.name: knownNetworkId
fields.doc: A saved network's `id`, instead of an SSID.

WifiNetworkInfo.summary: The network the device is on.

fields.name: capabilities
fields.doc: What this platform can do. Calls outside it fail with 501.

fields.name: current
fields.doc: The network the device is on, where the platform can tell.

fields.name: hotspotSupported
fields.doc: Whether the app registered the hotspot and the platform supports one.
